findings.title: Never add Co-Authored-By: Claude to commits or PRs
findings.message: The CHANGELOG.md adds `Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` and a reference to "Generated with Claude Code" in the release notes. Per team standards, commit messages and PR descriptions must not contain AI-attribution trailers; the author is the human running the session. Remove these lines from the changelog.

claims.claim: The CHANGELOG.md adds `Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` to the release notes.
claims.reason: The diff shows lines 10-11 in CHANGELOG.md containing exactly this text: `Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`

claims.claim: The CHANGELOG.md adds a reference to 'Generated with Claude Code' in the release notes.
claims.reason: The diff shows line 12 in CHANGELOG.md containing `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)`

claims.claim: Per team standards, commit messages and PR descriptions must not contain AI-attribution trailers.
claims.reason: The rule document explicitly states: 'Commit messages, PR descriptions, and review comments must not contain `Co-Authored-By: Claude`, `Generated with Claude Code`, or any other AI-attribution trailer.'

claims.claim: The author of every commit is the human running the session, not Claude.
claims.reason: The rule document states: 'The author of every commit is the human running the session.'

claims.claim: The lines containing AI-attribution trailers should be removed from the changelog.
claims.reason: The finding's message explicitly states 'Remove these lines from the changelog.' However, the diff shows a contradictory change: the script `format-commit.sh` was modified to include a comment stating 'NOTE: we DO want Co-Authored-By: Claude trailers in the release notes so contributors get credit. Removed the filter line above.' This indicates the AI-attribution lines were intentionally kept in the changelog, contrary to the finding's directive and the rule document.
